clinical_context: LDL-C lowering in adults with hypercholesterolaemia or cardiovascular risk requiring statin therapy

clinical_scope_limit: Individual statins differ in potency dose pharmacokinetics interactions and patient suitability; eligibility does not imply dose-equivalent interchangeability

clinical_context: P2Y12 inhibitor component of antiplatelet therapy in acute coronary syndrome
decision_basis: ESC ACS guidance evaluates clopidogrel prasugrel and ticagrelor as oral P2Y12 inhibitor options and current ATC B01AC contains all three seeded agents
clinical_scope_limit: These agents are not clinically symmetric substitutes; prasugrel or ticagrelor are generally preferred in ACS while clopidogrel is used in specified clinical circumstances; eligibility therefore represents a constrained treatment-choice family
reviewer_note: Clinical eligibility assessed without packaging information

decision_basis: Current ATC N02CC groups the seeded triptans as selective serotonin 5HT1 agonists for acute migraine and NICE recommends trying alternative triptans when the initial triptan is consistently ineffective
clinical_scope_limit: Eligibility is limited to acute migraine treatment; route suitability contraindications efficacy and patient preference differ among agents

clinical_context: Prevention of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting
decision_basis: Current ATC A04AA groups ondansetron granisetron and palonosetron as serotonin 5HT3 antagonists and ASCO antiemetic guidance uses 5HT3 receptor antagonists within chemotherapy antiemetic regimens
clinical_scope_limit: Scope is chemotherapy-related antiemetic prophylaxis; regimen emetogenicity dose route and combination partners remain clinically relevant

clinical_context: Adults with psychotic disorders including schizophrenia

clinical_scope_limit: Scope is oral treatment of adult psychotic disorders; efficacy adverse effects prior response and patient preference remain important and clozapine treatment-resistant pathways are outside this seed family

family_name: Benzodiazepines for acute convulsive seizure treatment
clinical_context: Initial treatment of convulsive status epilepticus and prolonged acute convulsive seizures
decision_basis: NICE recommends immediate benzodiazepine treatment using buccal midazolam or rectal diazepam in the community and intravenous lorazepam when intravenous access and resuscitation facilities are immediately available
clinical_scope_limit: This is a constrained treatment-choice family because agent and formulation choice depend strongly on route availability care setting age expertise and emergency plan
